verdict.what: a Japanese-style farmhouse with a dark tiled roof and flared eaves
verdict.style: Japanese minka or Edo-period countryside house, dark timber and tile
verdict.looks: A single-storey house on a raised base. The roof is the dominant mass: a wide, dark grey-black stepped tile roof with upturned, stair-stepped eave ends on the gable sides and a small dark chimney block. The walls are dark spruce or dark oak logs and planks, with light-grey window panes set in dark frames, a lighter timber band across the lower wall, and lanterns hung beside the entry. The base is cobblestone and mossy stone on a grass-topped dirt plinth, with a few patches of moss and vine across the stone. The entry has a short stone stair leading to a timber step and a stone pillar with a lantern on the front-left corner. On the side view the lower wall is slightly splayed and a dark timber post stands at the rear corner. The back and side walls are plainer, with fewer openings.
verdict.summary: This reads as a proper Japanese farmhouse: the flared dark tile roof and lanterns sell the style at a glance, the mossy stone base is a deliberate weathered choice, and it only needs the side and back walls given more openings and depth to feel finished.
